items.name: Artificial Intelligence
items.explanation: AI teaches computers to think, learn, and make decisions like humans

items.name: Machine Learning
items.explanation: ML lets computers learn from data without being explicitly programmed for every task

items.name: Neural Networks
items.explanation: Neural networks are inspired by the brain and learn to recognize patterns in data

items.name: Deep Learning
items.explanation: Deep learning stacks many neural network layers to solve complex AI problems

items.name: Computer Vision
items.explanation: Computer vision lets machines see and understand images and video like humans do

items.name: NLP
items.explanation: Natural Language Processing helps computers read, understand, and generate human language

items.name: Reinforcement Learning
items.explanation: RL trains AI by rewarding good decisions like teaching a dog new tricks with treats

items.name: Generative AI
items.explanation: Generative AI creates new content: text, images, audio, code, and video from scratch

items.name: Transfer Learning
items.explanation: Transfer learning reuses knowledge from one AI task to speed up solving another

items.name: AI Agents
items.explanation: AI agents can reason, plan, and take actions autonomously to complete complex tasks

items.name: Supervised Learning
items.explanation: Supervised learning trains AI using labeled examples with known correct answers

items.name: Unsupervised Learning
items.explanation: Unsupervised learning finds hidden patterns in data without any labeled examples

items.name: Semi-supervised Learning
items.explanation: Semi-supervised learning uses a small amount of labeled data plus lots of unlabeled data

items.name: Self-supervised Learning
items.explanation: Self-supervised learning creates its own labels from raw data to train on

items.name: Federated Learning
items.explanation: Federated learning trains AI across many devices without sharing private data centrally

items.name: Active Learning
items.explanation: Active learning lets the AI ask for labels on the examples it finds most confusing

items.name: Few-shot Learning
items.explanation: Few-shot learning teaches AI to recognize new concepts from just a handful of examples

items.name: Zero-shot Learning
items.explanation: Zero-shot learning allows AI to handle tasks it was never explicitly trained on

items.name: One-shot Learning
items.explanation: One-shot learning trains a model to recognize something from a single example

items.name: Meta-learning
items.explanation: Meta-learning teaches AI how to learn new tasks faster — it learns to learn

items.name: Explainable AI
items.explanation: XAI makes AI decisions transparent and understandable to humans

items.name: AI Safety
items.explanation: AI safety research ensures powerful AI systems remain aligned with human values and goals

items.name: AI Alignment
items.explanation: Alignment ensures that what AI optimizes for matches what humans actually want

items.name: AI Ethics
items.explanation: AI ethics studies the moral implications of building and deploying AI systems

items.name: Bias in AI
items.explanation: AI bias happens when training data contains unfair patterns that the model learns and repeats

items.name: AI Fairness
items.explanation: AI fairness ensures models treat all groups of people equitably without discrimination

items.name: Robustness
items.explanation: Robust AI performs reliably even when inputs are noisy, unusual, or adversarial

items.name: Adversarial Examples
items.explanation: Adversarial examples are inputs carefully crafted to fool AI models into making mistakes

items.name: Model Interpretability
items.explanation: Interpretability explains why an AI model produced a specific output or prediction

items.name: Feature Engineering
items.explanation: Feature engineering transforms raw data into meaningful inputs that help AI learn better

items.name: Overfitting
items.explanation: Overfitting is when a model memorizes training data but fails to generalize to new examples

items.name: Underfitting
items.explanation: Underfitting happens when a model is too simple to capture patterns in the training data

items.name: Regularization
items.explanation: Regularization adds penalties to prevent AI models from becoming too complex and overfitting

items.name: Cross-validation
items.explanation: Cross-validation tests model performance across different subsets of the data for reliability

items.name: Hyperparameter Tuning
items.explanation: Hyperparameter tuning finds the best settings to maximize an AI model's performance

items.name: Gradient Descent
items.explanation: Gradient descent is the algorithm that iteratively adjusts model weights to minimize error

items.name: Backpropagation
items.explanation: Backpropagation calculates how much each weight contributed to an error and adjusts accordingly

items.name: Epoch
items.explanation: An epoch is one complete pass through the entire training dataset during model training

items.name: Batch Size
items.explanation: Batch size is how many training examples the model processes before updating its weights

items.name: Learning Rate
items.explanation: The learning rate controls how big each step is when updating model weights during training

items.name: Dropout
items.explanation: Dropout randomly deactivates neurons during training to prevent overfitting

items.name: Attention Mechanism
items.explanation: Attention lets AI models focus on the most relevant parts of input when producing output

items.name: Convolutional Neural Net
items.explanation: CNNs use filters to detect visual patterns making them ideal for image recognition tasks

items.name: Recurrent Neural Net
items.explanation: RNNs process sequences step by step and maintain memory across time

items.name: LSTM
items.explanation: Long Short-Term Memory networks solve the vanishing gradient problem in long sequences

items.name: GAN
items.explanation: Generative Adversarial Networks pit a generator against a discriminator to create realistic content

items.name: Diffusion Model
items.explanation: Diffusion models generate images by learning to reverse a gradual noising process

items.name: Variational Autoencoder
items.explanation: VAEs compress data into a latent space and generate new examples by sampling from it

items.name: Encoder-Decoder
items.explanation: Encoder-decoder architectures compress input then reconstruct or translate it into output

items.name: Object Detection
items.explanation: Object detection identifies and draws bounding boxes around multiple objects in images

items.name: Image Segmentation
items.explanation: Image segmentation labels every pixel in an image with a class it belongs to

items.name: Speech Recognition
items.explanation: Speech recognition converts spoken audio into text as accurately as a human transcriber

items.name: Text-to-Speech
items.explanation: TTS synthesizes natural-sounding speech audio from plain text input

items.name: Sentiment Analysis
items.explanation: Sentiment analysis detects whether text is positive, negative, or neutral in tone

items.name: Named Entity Recognition
items.explanation: NER identifies and classifies names, dates, places, and organizations in text

items.name: Text Classification
items.explanation: Text classification automatically assigns categories or labels to pieces of text

items.name: Recommendation System
items.explanation: Recommendation systems predict what a user will like based on their history and behavior

items.name: Anomaly Detection
items.explanation: Anomaly detection identifies unusual patterns that deviate from normal expected behavior

items.name: Time Series Forecasting
items.explanation: AI forecasting models predict future values based on patterns in historical time data

items.name: Clustering
items.explanation: Clustering groups similar data points together without using any predefined labels

items.name: Principal Component Analysis
items.explanation: PCA reduces data dimensions while preserving the most important patterns and variance

items.name: Random Forest
items.explanation: Random forests combine many decision trees to make more accurate and stable predictions

items.name: Support Vector Machine
items.explanation: SVMs find the best boundary to separate classes with the maximum possible margin

items.name: Decision Tree
items.explanation: Decision trees make predictions by asking a series of yes or no questions about the data

items.name: Naive Bayes
items.explanation: Naive Bayes is a simple probabilistic classifier based on Bayes theorem for fast predictions

items.name: K-Nearest Neighbors
items.explanation: KNN classifies new data points based on what category their closest neighbors belong to

items.name: Logistic Regression
items.explanation: Logistic regression predicts the probability of a binary outcome from input features

items.name: Linear Regression
items.explanation: Linear regression models the straight-line relationship between input variables and output

items.name: Ensemble Learning
items.explanation: Ensemble methods combine multiple models to achieve better performance than any single one

items.name: Boosting
items.explanation: Boosting trains models sequentially where each one corrects the errors of the previous

items.name: Bagging
items.explanation: Bagging trains multiple models on random subsets and averages their predictions

items.name: Stacking
items.explanation: Stacking trains a meta-model on the outputs of multiple base models for better accuracy

items.name: Confusion Matrix
items.explanation: A confusion matrix shows how many predictions were correct and which errors were made

items.name: Precision and Recall
items.explanation: Precision measures accuracy of positive predictions while recall measures how many were found

items.name: F1 Score
items.explanation: The F1 score balances precision and recall into a single model performance metric

items.name: ROC Curve
items.explanation: The ROC curve shows the tradeoff between true positive rate and false positive rate

items.name: AUC
items.explanation: AUC measures overall model quality — a perfect model scores 1.0 on the AUC scale

items.name: Mean Squared Error
items.explanation: MSE averages the squared differences between predictions and actual values

items.name: Cross-entropy Loss
items.explanation: Cross-entropy loss measures how different predicted probabilities are from true labels

items.name: Reward Function
items.explanation: A reward function tells a reinforcement learning agent how good or bad an action was

items.name: Policy Gradient
items.explanation: Policy gradient methods optimize the AI policy directly using gradient ascent

items.name: Q-Learning
items.explanation: Q-learning teaches agents the value of taking actions in states to maximize future reward

items.name: Multi-agent Systems
items.explanation: Multi-agent AI has multiple intelligent agents collaborating or competing in an environment

items.name: Symbolic AI
items.explanation: Symbolic AI uses explicit rules and logic rather than learning from data

items.name: Neuro-symbolic AI
items.explanation: Neuro-symbolic AI combines neural learning with logical reasoning for explainable intelligence

items.name: Causal Inference
items.explanation: Causal AI understands cause and effect rather than just correlations in data

items.name: AutoML
items.explanation: AutoML automatically selects and tunes the best machine learning pipeline for a task

items.name: Neural Architecture Search
items.explanation: NAS automatically discovers the optimal neural network structure for a problem

items.name: Knowledge Graph
items.explanation: Knowledge graphs store facts as interconnected entities and relationships for AI reasoning

items.name: Ontology
items.explanation: Ontologies define structured vocabularies of concepts and their relationships in a domain

items.name: Data Augmentation
items.explanation: Data augmentation creates additional training examples by transforming existing ones

items.name: Synthetic Data
items.explanation: Synthetic data is AI-generated training data that mimics real data without privacy risks

items.name: Model Compression
items.explanation: Model compression reduces AI model size for deployment on edge devices with limited resources

items.name: Quantization
items.explanation: Quantization reduces model weight precision from 32-bit to 8-bit or 4-bit for speed and size

items.name: Pruning
items.explanation: Pruning removes unimportant neurons or weights from a neural network to make it leaner

items.name: Knowledge Distillation
items.explanation: Distillation trains a small student model to mimic the behavior of a large teacher model

items.name: Edge AI
items.explanation: Edge AI runs machine learning models directly on devices rather than in the cloud

items.name: Multimodal AI
items.explanation: Multimodal AI understands and generates multiple types of data like text, images, and audio

items.name: World Model
items.explanation: World models let AI simulate and predict outcomes in an environment to plan ahead

items.name: AI Benchmark
items.explanation: Benchmarks are standardized tests to measure and compare AI model capabilities fairly

items.name: Large Language Model
items.explanation: LLMs are AI trained on massive text data to understand and generate human language

items.name: Transformer
items.explanation: The Transformer architecture revolutionized AI with powerful self-attention mechanisms

items.name: Tokens
items.explanation: Tokens are the smallest text units LLMs process — roughly 0.75 words per token

items.name: Context Window
items.explanation: The context window is how much text an LLM can read and remember in one conversation

items.name: Prompt Engineering
items.explanation: Prompt engineering is crafting inputs to reliably get the best outputs from LLMs

items.name: Fine-tuning
items.explanation: Fine-tuning adapts a pre-trained LLM to a specific domain, task, or writing style

items.name: Embeddings
items.explanation: Embeddings are numerical vectors that capture the meaning of text for AI search and retrieval

items.name: Hallucination
items.explanation: LLM hallucination is when the model generates confident but factually incorrect answers

items.name: Temperature
items.explanation: Temperature controls how creative or random an LLM's output is — higher means more creative

items.name: System Prompt
items.explanation: A system prompt sets the AI assistant's role, persona, rules, and constraints upfront

items.name: Pre-training
items.explanation: Pre-training is the initial phase where a model learns language patterns from massive text corpora

items.name: RLHF
items.explanation: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback aligns LLMs to human preferences and values

items.name: RLAIF
items.explanation: RLAIF uses AI feedback instead of human feedback to align language models at scale

items.name: Constitutional AI
items.explanation: Constitutional AI trains models using a set of principles to guide safe and helpful behavior

items.name: Instruction Tuning
items.explanation: Instruction tuning trains LLMs to follow natural language instructions reliably

items.name: Chain-of-Thought
items.explanation: Chain-of-thought prompting makes LLMs reason step by step for more accurate answers

items.name: Few-shot Prompting
items.explanation: Few-shot prompting gives the LLM several examples in the prompt to guide its responses

items.name: Zero-shot Prompting
items.explanation: Zero-shot prompting asks the LLM to complete a task with no examples given

items.name: Top-p Sampling
items.explanation: Top-p (nucleus) sampling limits word choices to the smallest set covering p probability mass

items.name: Top-k Sampling
items.explanation: Top-k sampling restricts the model to only choose from the k most likely next tokens

items.name: Beam Search
items.explanation: Beam search keeps multiple candidate sequences and picks the most probable final output

items.name: Greedy Decoding
items.explanation: Greedy decoding always picks the single most likely next token at every step

items.name: Tokenizer
items.explanation: A tokenizer converts text into numerical tokens that the model can process

items.name: Vocabulary
items.explanation: An LLM vocabulary is the complete set of tokens the model knows and can use

items.name: Attention Head
items.explanation: Attention heads each learn to focus on different relationships within the input text

items.name: Multi-head Attention
items.explanation: Multi-head attention runs several attention operations in parallel for richer representations

items.name: Positional Encoding
items.explanation: Positional encoding tells the Transformer where each token appears in the sequence

items.name: Layer Normalization
items.explanation: Layer normalization stabilizes training by normalizing activations within each layer

items.name: Feed-forward Layer
items.explanation: Feed-forward layers in Transformers process each token's representation independently

items.name: Residual Connection
items.explanation: Residual connections let information skip layers to prevent vanishing gradients in deep models

items.name: Model Weights
items.explanation: Model weights are billions of numerical parameters that store everything the LLM has learned

items.name: Parameter Count
items.explanation: Parameter count measures model size — larger models generally have greater capability

items.name: Scaling Law
items.explanation: Scaling laws predict how model performance improves with more data, compute, and parameters

items.name: Emergent Abilities
items.explanation: Emergent abilities are surprising capabilities that appear as LLMs scale up in size

items.name: In-context Learning
items.explanation: In-context learning lets LLMs learn new tasks from examples provided directly in the prompt

items.name: Prompt Injection
items.explanation: Prompt injection attacks try to hijack an AI's behavior using malicious input text

items.name: Jailbreaking
items.explanation: Jailbreaking tries to bypass an LLM's safety guidelines through clever prompting

items.name: Guardrails
items.explanation: Guardrails are safety checks that prevent LLMs from generating harmful or inappropriate content

items.name: GGUF Format
items.explanation: GGUF is a file format for storing quantized LLMs for efficient local deployment

items.name: Mixture of Experts
items.explanation: MoE architecture activates only a subset of model parameters per token for efficient scaling

items.name: Sparse Attention
items.explanation: Sparse attention computes only a subset of attention scores to handle very long contexts

items.name: Flash Attention
items.explanation: Flash Attention is a hardware-aware algorithm that makes Transformer training much faster

items.name: KV Cache
items.explanation: The KV cache stores computed attention keys and values to speed up text generation

items.name: Speculative Decoding
items.explanation: Speculative decoding uses a small draft model to speed up generation by the larger model

items.name: Sliding Window Attention
items.explanation: Sliding window attention lets models handle longer contexts by attending to nearby tokens

items.name: Rotary Embeddings
items.explanation: RoPE encodes position information in a way that generalizes to longer sequences

items.name: Grouped Query Attention
items.explanation: GQA reduces memory and computation by sharing key-value heads across query heads

items.name: Perplexity
items.explanation: Perplexity measures how well an LLM predicts text — lower means more confident and accurate

items.name: BLEU Score
items.explanation: BLEU score measures how closely AI-generated text matches human reference translations

items.name: ROUGE Score
items.explanation: ROUGE measures overlap between AI-generated summaries and human-written reference summaries

items.name: BenchMark Evaluation
items.explanation: Benchmarks like MMLU and HellaSwag measure LLM knowledge and reasoning across many subjects

items.name: MMLU
items.explanation: Massive Multitask Language Understanding tests LLMs across 57 academic subjects

items.name: HumanEval
items.explanation: HumanEval benchmarks LLM coding ability by asking them to write and pass real Python tests

items.name: GSM8K
items.explanation: GSM8K tests grade school math reasoning requiring multi-step problem solving

items.name: TruthfulQA
items.explanation: TruthfulQA tests whether LLMs give honest accurate answers instead of plausible-sounding falsehoods

items.name: LoRA
items.explanation: Low-Rank Adaptation fine-tunes LLMs efficiently by training only small adapter layers

items.name: QLoRA
items.explanation: QLoRA combines quantization and LoRA to fine-tune large models on consumer hardware

items.name: PEFT
items.explanation: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning updates only a small fraction of model parameters to save compute

items.name: Adapter Layers
items.explanation: Adapter layers add small trainable modules between frozen pre-trained model layers

items.name: Prefix Tuning
items.explanation: Prefix tuning prepends trainable virtual tokens to the input instead of updating model weights

items.name: Prompt Tuning
items.explanation: Prompt tuning learns soft prompt embeddings while keeping the full model frozen

items.name: Tokenization
items.explanation: Tokenization splits text into subword pieces using algorithms like BPE or WordPiece

items.name: BPE
items.explanation: Byte Pair Encoding builds a vocabulary by iteratively merging the most frequent character pairs

items.name: SentencePiece
items.explanation: SentencePiece is a language-independent tokenization library used by many modern LLMs

items.name: Padding
items.explanation: Padding adds dummy tokens to make all sequences the same length in a batch

items.name: Truncation
items.explanation: Truncation cuts sequences that exceed the maximum context length of the model

items.name: Logits
items.explanation: Logits are raw unnormalized scores the model assigns to each possible next token

items.name: Softmax
items.explanation: Softmax converts logits into a probability distribution over the vocabulary

items.name: Cross-attention
items.explanation: Cross-attention lets the decoder attend to encoder representations in sequence-to-sequence tasks

items.name: Causal Masking
items.explanation: Causal masking prevents the model from attending to future tokens during training

items.name: Inference
items.explanation: Inference is the process of running a trained LLM to generate predictions or responses

items.name: Quantization LLM
items.explanation: Quantization reduces LLM weight precision to run large models on smaller hardware

items.name: Tensor Parallelism
items.explanation: Tensor parallelism splits model tensors across multiple GPUs to fit very large models

items.name: Pipeline Parallelism
items.explanation: Pipeline parallelism splits model layers across GPUs so each GPU handles different layers

items.name: Model Serving
items.explanation: Model serving hosts LLMs in production to handle real-time inference requests at scale

items.name: vLLM
items.explanation: vLLM is an efficient LLM inference engine using PagedAttention for high throughput serving

items.name: Ollama
items.explanation: Ollama lets you run open-source LLMs locally on your laptop with a simple command

items.name: LLaMA
items.explanation: Meta's LLaMA is an open-weight large language model series used by researchers worldwide

items.name: GPT
items.explanation: GPT (Generative Pre-trained Transformer) is OpenAI's family of influential language models

items.name: Claude
items.explanation: Claude is Anthropic's AI assistant family trained to be helpful, harmless, and honest

items.name: Gemini
items.explanation: Gemini is Google DeepMind's multimodal AI model family competing with GPT and Claude

items.name: Mistral
items.explanation: Mistral is a French AI startup making efficient high-quality open-weight language models

items.name: Phi
items.explanation: Microsoft's Phi models are surprisingly capable small language models trained on high-quality data

items.name: Qwen
items.explanation: Qwen is Alibaba's family of open-weight multilingual large language models

items.name: DeepSeek
items.explanation: DeepSeek is a Chinese LLM series that achieved GPT-4-level performance at far lower cost

items.name: Reward Model
items.explanation: A reward model scores LLM outputs for quality, helpfulness, and safety during RLHF training

items.name: Constitutional Principles
items.explanation: Constitutional principles are explicit rules an AI uses to critique and improve its own outputs

items.name: Red-teaming
items.explanation: Red-teaming adversarially tests LLMs to find safety failures before deployment

items.name: Model Card
items.explanation: A model card documents what an AI model can do, how it was trained, and known limitations

items.name: System 2 Thinking
items.explanation: System 2 AI mimics slow deliberate reasoning rather than fast instinctive responses

items.name: Reasoning Model
items.explanation: Reasoning models think step by step internally before producing a final answer

items.name: Mixture of Experts Routing
items.explanation: MoE routing gates select which expert sub-networks handle each input token dynamically

items.name: Sliding Context
items.explanation: Sliding context moves a fixed-size window across very long documents for extended processing

items.name: Long Context LLM
items.explanation: Long context models like Gemini 1.5 can process over a million tokens in one pass

items.name: Prompt Caching
items.explanation: Prompt caching stores computed activations for repeated prompt prefixes to save cost and latency

items.name: Structured Output LLM
items.explanation: Structured output forces LLMs to respond in valid JSON or a specified schema every time

items.name: Function Calling
items.explanation: Function calling lets LLMs invoke structured external functions based on natural language requests

items.name: Tool Use
items.explanation: Tool use enables LLMs to call external APIs, search the web, and run code during reasoning

items.name: Multi-turn Conversation
items.explanation: Multi-turn conversations maintain context across many message exchanges in a session

items.name: Safety Training
items.explanation: Safety training teaches LLMs to refuse harmful requests and add caveats to dangerous content

items.name: RAG
items.explanation: Retrieval Augmented Generation combines search with LLMs to give accurate grounded answers

items.name: Vector Database
items.explanation: Vector databases store embeddings and enable lightning-fast semantic similarity search

items.name: Chunking
items.explanation: Chunking splits documents into smaller pieces for efficient storage and relevant retrieval

items.name: Semantic Search
items.explanation: Semantic search finds results by meaning not just keyword matching — much smarter

items.name: Re-ranking
items.explanation: Re-ranking re-orders retrieved results to improve relevance before passing them to the LLM

items.name: Knowledge Base
items.explanation: A knowledge base is your collection of documents that RAG searches to answer questions

items.name: Document Loader
items.explanation: Document loaders parse PDFs, web pages, and files into clean text for RAG pipelines

items.name: Query Expansion
items.explanation: Query expansion rewrites user questions multiple ways to improve search recall and coverage

items.name: Hybrid Search
items.explanation: Hybrid search combines keyword and semantic search for better more reliable results

items.name: Context Window RAG
items.explanation: RAG stuffs retrieved documents into the LLM's context so it can answer with real knowledge

items.name: Naive RAG
items.explanation: Naive RAG indexes documents, retrieves top-k chunks, and feeds them to an LLM without optimization

items.name: Advanced RAG
items.explanation: Advanced RAG adds pre-retrieval and post-retrieval steps to dramatically improve answer quality

items.name: Modular RAG
items.explanation: Modular RAG is a flexible framework where each pipeline component can be swapped independently

items.name: Agentic RAG
items.explanation: Agentic RAG uses an AI agent that decides when and how to retrieve information dynamically

items.name: Self-RAG
items.explanation: Self-RAG trains the model to decide when to retrieve and to critique its own generated answers

items.name: Corrective RAG
items.explanation: Corrective RAG evaluates retrieved documents and web-searches for more if they are not relevant

items.name: Sentence-window Retrieval
items.explanation: Sentence-window retrieval stores small sentences but returns the surrounding context window

items.name: Parent-child Chunking
items.explanation: Parent-child chunking retrieves small child chunks but passes larger parent context to the LLM

items.name: Recursive Chunking
items.explanation: Recursive chunking splits text hierarchically using natural boundaries like paragraphs and sentences

items.name: Semantic Chunking
items.explanation: Semantic chunking splits documents at points where the topic meaningfully changes

items.name: Fixed-size Chunking
items.explanation: Fixed-size chunking splits documents into equal token or character length pieces

items.name: Overlapping Chunks
items.explanation: Overlapping chunks share text between adjacent pieces so context is never split abruptly

items.name: Sparse Retrieval
items.explanation: Sparse retrieval uses keyword signals like BM25 to find lexically matching documents

items.name: Dense Retrieval
items.explanation: Dense retrieval uses embedding similarity to find semantically relevant documents

items.name: BM25
items.explanation: BM25 is a classic keyword ranking algorithm that scores documents by term frequency

items.name: FAISS
items.explanation: FAISS is Meta's fast similarity search library for finding nearest vectors at scale

items.name: Pinecone
items.explanation: Pinecone is a managed vector database built for production AI applications

items.name: Weaviate
items.explanation: Weaviate is an open-source vector database with a built-in hybrid search capability

items.name: Chroma
items.explanation: Chroma is a lightweight open-source vector database popular for local RAG development

items.name: Qdrant
items.explanation: Qdrant is a high-performance vector database with advanced filtering capabilities

items.name: Milvus
items.explanation: Milvus is a scalable open-source vector database designed for enterprise AI workloads

items.name: LanceDB
items.explanation: LanceDB is a developer-friendly embedded vector database that runs locally

items.name: Embedding Model
items.explanation: Embedding models convert text into dense numerical vectors that capture semantic meaning

items.name: Bi-encoder
items.explanation: Bi-encoders create independent embeddings for queries and documents for fast retrieval

items.name: Cross-encoder
items.explanation: Cross-encoders compare query and document together for highly accurate re-ranking

items.name: HNSW
items.explanation: Hierarchical Navigable Small World is a fast graph algorithm for approximate nearest neighbor search

items.name: ANN Search
items.explanation: Approximate Nearest Neighbor search trades perfect accuracy for massive speed gains

items.name: Cosine Similarity
items.explanation: Cosine similarity measures the angle between two vectors to quantify how similar they are

items.name: Dot Product
items.explanation: Dot product similarity multiplies corresponding embedding dimensions and sums the results

items.name: L2 Distance
items.explanation: L2 or Euclidean distance measures the straight-line distance between two embedding vectors

items.name: Namespace
items.explanation: Namespaces partition a vector index so different users or tenants have isolated data

items.name: Metadata Filtering
items.explanation: Metadata filtering restricts vector search to documents matching specific tags or fields

items.name: Multi-vector Retrieval
items.explanation: Multi-vector retrieval represents each document with multiple embeddings for better coverage

items.name: ColBERT
items.explanation: ColBERT stores token-level embeddings per document enabling late interaction for accurate retrieval

items.name: HyDE
items.explanation: HyDE generates a hypothetical document answer and uses that embedding to search for real ones

items.name: Query Routing
items.explanation: Query routing directs different questions to the most appropriate retrieval pipeline

items.name: Ensemble Retrieval
items.explanation: Ensemble retrieval combines results from multiple retrievers and fuses their scores

items.name: Reciprocal Rank Fusion
items.explanation: RRF combines ranked lists from multiple retrievers into a single better-performing ranked list

items.name: Contextual Compression
items.explanation: Contextual compression extracts only the most relevant sentences from retrieved documents

items.name: LLM Re-ranker
items.explanation: An LLM re-ranker scores retrieved passages by asking the model which best answers the query

items.name: Cohere Rerank
items.explanation: Cohere Rerank is a powerful API for improving search result relevance with a cross-encoder

items.name: Lost in the Middle
items.explanation: LLMs perform worse on information placed in the middle of long contexts versus edges

items.name: Answer Generation
items.explanation: Answer generation is the final RAG step where the LLM synthesizes retrieved chunks into a response

items.name: Citation Generation
items.explanation: RAG systems can cite source documents in answers so users can verify the information

items.name: Grounding
items.explanation: Grounding anchors LLM responses to retrieved factual sources to reduce hallucination

items.name: Faithfulness
items.explanation: Faithfulness measures whether a RAG answer is actually supported by the retrieved documents

items.name: Answer Relevance
items.explanation: Answer relevance measures whether the generated answer actually addresses the question asked

items.name: Context Recall
items.explanation: Context recall measures whether retrieved chunks contain all information needed to answer

items.name: RAGAS
items.explanation: RAGAS is an evaluation framework that automatically scores RAG pipelines on key quality metrics

items.explanation: HIPAA requires cloud services handling US medical records to meet strict security standards

items.name: Zero Trust
items.explanation: Zero trust security assumes no user or system is trusted by default even inside the network

items.name: VPN
items.explanation: A VPN creates an encrypted private tunnel between your network and the cloud

items.name: Direct Connect
items.explanation: AWS Direct Connect provides dedicated private network connections from your data center to AWS

items.name: PoP

items.name: Egress Cost

items.name: eBPF

items.name: WebAssembly Cloud
items.explanation: WebAssembly on the cloud runs portable sandboxed code at the edge with near-native performance

items.name: Cloud Migration

items.name: Lift and Shift
items.explanation: Lift and shift moves applications to the cloud without changing their architecture

items.name: Re-platforming
items.explanation: Re-platforming makes minor cloud optimizations during migration like switching to managed databases

items.name: Re-architecting
items.explanation: Re-architecting redesigns applications to fully leverage cloud-native services and patterns

items.name: Cloud Bursting
items.explanation: Cloud bursting runs workloads on-premises normally and spills to the cloud during peak demand

items.name: Managed Service
items.explanation: Managed services let the cloud provider handle provisioning, patching, and scaling for you

items.name: Serverless Framework
items.explanation: Serverless Framework is an open-source tool for deploying serverless functions across cloud providers

items.name: AWS SAM
items.explanation: AWS Serverless Application Model simplifies building and deploying serverless apps on AWS

items.name: Infrastructure Drift

items.name: Cloud Security Posture
items.explanation: CSPM tools continuously monitor cloud configurations for security misconfigurations

items.name: Cybersecurity
items.explanation: Cybersecurity protects computers, networks, and data from attacks, theft, and unauthorized access

items.name: Encryption
items.explanation: Encryption scrambles data so only authorized parties with the key can read it

items.name: Firewall
items.explanation: A firewall monitors and controls incoming and outgoing network traffic based on security rules

items.name: VPN
items.explanation: A VPN creates an encrypted tunnel protecting your internet traffic from surveillance

items.name: Two-factor Authentication
items.explanation: 2FA requires a second proof of identity beyond your password to access an account

items.name: Phishing
items.explanation: Phishing tricks people into revealing credentials or clicking malware links via fake messages

items.name: Malware
items.explanation: Malware is software designed to damage, disrupt, or gain unauthorized access to computer systems

items.name: Ransomware
items.explanation: Ransomware encrypts your files and demands payment to restore access to them

items.name: Zero-day
items.explanation: A zero-day vulnerability is an undiscovered flaw that hackers exploit before a patch exists

items.name: Penetration Testing
items.explanation: Pen testing simulates real attacks to find and fix security weaknesses before hackers do

items.name: SQL Injection
items.explanation: SQL injection inserts malicious code into database queries to steal or modify data

items.name: XSS
items.explanation: Cross-site scripting injects malicious scripts into web pages viewed by other users

items.name: CSRF
items.explanation: Cross-site request forgery tricks a browser into making unauthorized requests to another site

items.name: DDoS
items.explanation: Distributed Denial of Service floods a server with traffic to make it unavailable

items.name: Man-in-the-Middle
items.explanation: MITM attacks intercept and potentially alter communications between two parties

items.name: Social Engineering
items.explanation: Social engineering manipulates people into giving up secrets or access instead of hacking systems

items.name: Brute Force Attack
items.explanation: Brute force attacks try every possible password combination until they find the right one

items.name: Credential Stuffing
items.explanation: Credential stuffing uses leaked username-password pairs from breaches on other sites

items.name: Public Key Infrastructure
items.explanation: PKI is a system of digital certificates and keys that enables secure encrypted communication

items.name: Certificate Authority
items.explanation: A CA issues digital certificates that verify a website's identity over HTTPS

items.name: RSA
items.explanation: RSA is a widely used public-key cryptographic algorithm for encryption and digital signing

items.name: AES
items.explanation: Advanced Encryption Standard is the gold standard symmetric encryption algorithm used worldwide

items.name: Hashing
items.explanation: Hashing converts data into a fixed-length digest that cannot be reversed to find the original

items.name: Salt
items.explanation: A cryptographic salt is random data added to passwords before hashing to prevent rainbow table attacks

items.name: Password Manager
items.explanation: A password manager generates and stores unique strong passwords for every account securely

items.name: Biometrics
items.explanation: Biometric authentication uses fingerprints, face, or iris scans instead of passwords

items.name: Single Sign-On
items.explanation: SSO lets users log into multiple apps with one set of credentials

items.name: SAML
items.explanation: SAML is an XML-based standard for exchanging authentication data between identity providers and apps

items.name: OIDC
items.explanation: OpenID Connect is an identity layer on top of OAuth 2.0 for authentication

items.name: Zero Trust Security
items.explanation: Zero trust never automatically trusts any user or device and verifies every access request

items.name: Least Privilege
items.explanation: Least privilege grants users and systems only the minimum permissions they need to function

items.name: Defense in Depth
items.explanation: Defense in depth layers multiple security controls so no single failure causes a breach

items.name: SIEM
items.explanation: Security Information and Event Management aggregates and analyzes logs to detect threats

items.name: SOAR
items.explanation: SOAR automates security incident response workflows to speed up threat neutralization

items.name: Threat Intelligence
items.explanation: Threat intelligence gathers information about current attackers and tactics to improve defenses

items.name: Vulnerability Scanner
items.explanation: Vulnerability scanners automatically probe systems to find known security weaknesses

items.name: CVSS
items.explanation: Common Vulnerability Scoring System rates the severity of security vulnerabilities from 0 to 10

items.name: CVE
items.explanation: Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures is a public dictionary of known security flaws

items.name: Bug Bounty
items.explanation: Bug bounty programs pay security researchers to responsibly disclose vulnerabilities

items.name: Responsible Disclosure
items.explanation: Responsible disclosure reports vulnerabilities privately to vendors before going public

items.name: WAF
items.explanation: A Web Application Firewall blocks malicious HTTP traffic targeting web application vulnerabilities

items.name: IDS
items.explanation: An Intrusion Detection System monitors network traffic and alerts on suspicious patterns

items.name: IPS
items.explanation: An Intrusion Prevention System actively blocks detected threats in real time

items.name: EDR
items.explanation: Endpoint Detection and Response monitors devices for threats and provides forensic investigation

items.name: XDR
items.explanation: Extended Detection and Response unifies security data across endpoints, network, and cloud

items.name: Security Audit
items.explanation: A security audit systematically reviews systems, policies, and controls for compliance and risk

items.name: Compliance
items.explanation: Security compliance meets regulatory standards like SOC2, HIPAA, and ISO 27001

items.name: GDPR
items.explanation: GDPR fines companies up to 4% of global revenue for mishandling European personal data

items.name: Data Breach
items.explanation: A data breach is unauthorized access to confidential data that exposes it to attackers

items.name: Insider Threat
items.explanation: Insider threats come from employees or contractors who misuse their legitimate access

items.name: Advanced Persistent Threat
items.explanation: APTs are sophisticated long-term attacks by nation-states or organized crime groups

items.name: Botnet
items.explanation: A botnet is a network of compromised computers controlled by attackers for DDoS or spam

items.name: Keylogger
items.explanation: Keyloggers secretly record every keystroke to steal passwords and sensitive data

items.name: Rootkit
items.explanation: Rootkits hide deep in operating systems to give attackers persistent undetected access

items.name: Backdoor
items.explanation: A backdoor is a hidden method of bypassing normal authentication to access a system

items.name: Exploit
items.explanation: An exploit is code or technique that takes advantage of a vulnerability to compromise a system

items.name: Payload
items.explanation: A payload is the malicious code that executes after an exploit successfully compromises a system

items.name: Command and Control
items.explanation: C2 servers remotely control malware installed on compromised victim machines

items.name: Exfiltration
items.explanation: Data exfiltration is the unauthorized transfer of sensitive data out of an organization

items.name: Lateral Movement
items.explanation: Lateral movement is when attackers spread through a network after gaining initial access

items.name: Privilege Escalation
items.explanation: Privilege escalation gains higher permissions than originally granted to access more systems

items.name: Supply Chain Attack
items.explanation: Supply chain attacks compromise software or hardware before it reaches the target organization

items.name: Homomorphic Encryption
items.explanation: Homomorphic encryption allows computations on encrypted data without ever decrypting it

items.name: End-to-End Encryption
items.explanation: E2EE ensures only sender and receiver can read messages — not even the service provider

items.name: Quantum Cryptography
items.explanation: Quantum cryptography uses quantum mechanics to create theoretically unbreakable encryption

items.name: Post-quantum Cryptography
items.explanation: Post-quantum algorithms are designed to resist attacks from future quantum computers

items.name: Hardware Security Module
items.explanation: HSMs are tamper-proof hardware devices that store and use cryptographic keys securely

items.name: Secure Boot
items.explanation: Secure boot verifies that only trusted software loads when a computer starts

items.name: TPM
items.explanation: Trusted Platform Module is a chip that stores cryptographic keys to secure device integrity

items.name: Memory Safety
items.explanation: Memory-safe languages like Rust prevent entire classes of security bugs at compile time

items.name: Buffer Overflow
items.explanation: Buffer overflows write beyond allocated memory to corrupt data or execute malicious code

items.name: Code Injection
items.explanation: Code injection inserts malicious commands into an application via unsanitized user input

items.name: Input Validation
items.explanation: Input validation checks all user-provided data before processing to prevent injection attacks

items.name: OWASP Top 10
items.explanation: OWASP Top 10 lists the most critical web application security risks developers must address

items.name: Security by Design
items.explanation: Security by design builds protection into systems from the start rather than adding it later

items.name: Shift Left Security
items.explanation: Shifting left integrates security testing early in the development lifecycle

items.name: DevSecOps
items.explanation: DevSecOps integrates security practices throughout the entire CI/CD pipeline

items.name: DAST
items.explanation: Dynamic Application Security Testing attacks running apps to find exploitable vulnerabilities

items.name: SAST
items.explanation: Static Application Security Testing analyzes source code for security flaws without running it

items.name: SCA
items.explanation: Software Composition Analysis identifies vulnerabilities in open-source dependencies

items.name: Container Scanning
items.explanation: Container image scanning detects known vulnerabilities in OS packages and dependencies

items.name: Secret Scanning
items.explanation: Secret scanning detects accidentally committed API keys and passwords in code repositories

items.name: Security Headers
items.explanation: HTTP security headers like CSP and HSTS instruct browsers to enforce additional protections

items.name: Content Security Policy
items.explanation: CSP prevents XSS by specifying which sources of scripts and content browsers should trust

items.name: HSTS
items.explanation: HTTP Strict Transport Security forces browsers to only connect via HTTPS

items.name: Cyber Kill Chain
items.explanation: The cyber kill chain models the stages of an attack from reconnaissance to data exfiltration

items.name: MITRE ATT&CK
items.explanation: MITRE ATT&CK is a framework cataloging real-world attacker tactics and techniques

items.name: Red Team
items.explanation: A red team simulates real attackers to test how well an organization can be compromised

items.name: Blue Team
items.explanation: A blue team defends against red team and real attacks by monitoring and responding to threats

items.name: Purple Team
items.explanation: Purple teaming combines red and blue teams to improve defenses through shared knowledge

items.name: Honeypot
items.explanation: A honeypot is a decoy system designed to attract and trap attackers to study their methods

items.name: Digital Forensics
items.explanation: Digital forensics recovers and analyzes evidence from devices after a security incident

items.name: Incident Response
items.explanation: Incident response is the structured process of containing and recovering from a security breach

items.name: Threat Modeling
items.explanation: Threat modeling systematically identifies potential threats to a system and designs mitigations

items.name: Attack Surface
items.explanation: The attack surface is the total number of entry points an attacker could use to compromise a system

items.name: Hardening
items.explanation: System hardening reduces the attack surface by disabling unneeded services and applying security settings

items.name: Patch Management
items.explanation: Patch management keeps software up to date with security fixes to close known vulnerabilities

items.name: Security Posture
items.explanation: Security posture is an organization's overall readiness to detect and respond to cyber threats

items.name: Canary Token
items.explanation: Canary tokens are fake credentials that alert you when attackers find and use them

items.name: Air Gap
items.explanation: An air-gapped system is completely isolated from the internet to protect highly sensitive data
